laws.rule: Glarus's rest-day law (Ruhetagsgesetz, arts 2 to 4 and 7): public rest days are Sundays; the general holidays (New Year's Day, the Näfels ride festival (Fahrtsfest), Easter Monday, Ascension, Whit Monday, 1 August, All Saints and St Stephen's Day); and the high holidays (Good Friday, Easter Sunday, Whit Sunday, the Federal Day of Prayer, and Christmas). On public rest days, activities that can disturb the quiet and dignity of the day are banned, including disturbing a church service, commercial activity that causes excessive noise, ordinary weekday work, fire-brigade drills and inspections, and unsolicited door-to-door selling. Shops and service businesses stay closed, subject to the federal Sunday-work exceptions. On high holidays, non-religious public assemblies and processions; concert, dance, theatre, film and trade-fair events that are not in closed rooms; sports events and related celebrations that are not in closed rooms; shooting practice; commercially run exhibitions that are not in closed rooms; car washes and amusement-arcade operations; and markets, shows and circuses that are not in closed rooms are also banned. Shops may open on the Näfels ride festival, on Landsgemeinde day in Glarus, and on the local parish-fair day. Communes may name at most four Sundays a year when shops may open. The Regierungsrat may allow shops and services to open on rest days in places of substantial tourist importance.
